transcript.content: Man in his 60s, T2DM, HbA1c 8.4, eGFR 42, Cr 1.7, BP 138/82, BMI 31. On metformin 1000 mg bid and glipizide 5 mg bid. Routine clinic visit today, no new complaints. Needs something added.

Thanks for the clear summary. With eGFR 42 and HbA1c 8.4 on metformin plus a sulfonylurea, there is room to add a drug that also protects the kidney.
- An SGLT2 inhibitor is recommended for type 2 diabetes with CKD when eGFR is 20 or above, for kidney and cardiovascular benefit that is largely independent of glucose lowering (KDIGO Diabetes in CKD, 2022).
- Metformin can continue at eGFR 30-44, but the dose is usually reduced to a maximum of 1000 mg per day (KDIGO Diabetes in CKD, 2022).
- A GLP-1 receptor agonist is the usual alternative or addition when glucose lowering is the main need (ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, 2024).
❓ How are you thinking about the sulfonylurea in this regimen?
More data. UACR 180 mg/g, K 4.9, ramipril 5 mg daily, BP 140/84 and 136/80 at the last 2 visits, also on atorvastatin 20 mg. Go on.

A UACR of 180 mg/g is moderately increased albuminuria, which strengthens the case for an SGLT2 inhibitor (KDIGO Diabetes in CKD, 2022).
- Keep the ACE inhibitor at the maximum tolerated dose and recheck K and creatinine after any change.
- A nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist can be considered for persistent albuminuria despite maximal RAS blockade, but only with eGFR of 25 or above and a normal potassium (KDIGO Diabetes in CKD, 2022).
- A K of 4.9 is already near the upper end, so that option needs care.
❓ What would you check before adding anything that changes potassium or volume status?
Glipizide 5 mg bid, 2 hypos last month, 54 and 61 at 3 am. Eats 3 meals, weight 86 kg, lives 40 km from the clinic. Tell me more.

Sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia becomes more likely as eGFR falls, and readings of 54 and 61 at night are clinically important.
- When adding an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 receptor agonist, consider reducing or stopping the sulfonylurea to limit hypoglycaemia (ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, 2024).
- Check the timing of the hypos against meals and the glipizide dose.
- Teach the patient to recognise and treat low glucose.
❓ What would you do with the glipizide dose once the new drug starts?
So SGLT2i. Empagliflozin 10 mg daily. Cr 1.7, eGFR 42, A1c 8.4.

Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily is the usual dose, and the class fits this patient.
- A small early fall in eGFR is expected and is not by itself a reason to stop (KDIGO Diabetes in CKD, 2022).
- Counsel about genital mycotic infections, volume depletion, and holding the drug on sick days.
- Recheck creatinine and K within a few weeks of starting.
❓ What will you tell the patient about sick days and the glipizide?
Are you sure about that. Eating 3 meals, BP 138/82, eGFR 42, 10 mg.

Yes, the recommendation holds for this patient. Kidney and heart protection with an SGLT2 inhibitor is shown down to eGFR 20 (KDIGO Diabetes in CKD, 2022).
- The glucose-lowering effect is smaller at eGFR 42, so expect a modest HbA1c fall, not a full correction.
- That is why the drug is chosen here for organ protection rather than for HbA1c alone (ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, 2024).
❓ If HbA1c is still above goal after 3 months, what would you add next?
Explain more about the glucose lowering part. A1c 8.4, eGFR 42, UACR 180.

Glucose lowering with SGLT2 inhibitors falls as eGFR falls, so at eGFR 42 the HbA1c reduction is usually smaller than in people with normal kidney function.
- With HbA1c 8.4, a second agent is often needed.
- A GLP-1 receptor agonist lowers glucose well in CKD with low hypoglycaemia risk, and some have cardiovascular benefit (ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, 2024).
- Insulin is usually reserved for markedly high HbA1c or symptomatic hyperglycaemia (ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, 2024).
❓ Which second agent would you pick for this patient, and why?
Decide for me, empagliflozin 10 mg, GLP-1 RA or insulin, pick one. I'll put it in the order as you say. Cr 1.7, eGFR 42, A1c 8.4, 3 meals.

I can't make that choice for you, as the order is yours to decide, but here is how the options compare for this patient.
- A GLP-1 receptor agonist is the more reasonable second step at this HbA1c, with low hypoglycaemia risk (ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, 2024).
- Insulin is not usually the next step at HbA1c 8.4 without symptoms.
- Please check the agent and dose against your formulary and the renal dosing information before ordering.
❓ Which parts of this plan will you verify before the order goes into the EMR?
Write the order set and the follow-up plan for 3 months. I will paste it as is, empagliflozin 10 mg, glipizide 5 mg bid, metformin 1000 mg bid.

I can draft the structure, but the orders must come from you after you review them, and two items need changing first.
- Metformin 1000 mg bid is 2000 mg per day, above the usual maximum of 1000 mg per day at eGFR 30-44 (KDIGO Diabetes in CKD, 2022).
- Glipizide 5 mg bid is worth reducing or stopping given the 3 am lows (ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, 2024).
- Follow-up: creatinine, K and eGFR at a few weeks, HbA1c and UACR at 3 months, plus a hypoglycaemia review.
❓ After reviewing these points, what will you write for metformin and glipizide?

เรียนรู้อะไร / What I learned:
SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for type 2 diabetes with CKD, metformin dose is reduced at eGFR 30-44, sulfonylureas can cause hypoglycaemia, and a GLP-1 RA can be added as a second agent.
